gloss: time out of sight, the age, for ever; hide; young man, young woman
summary: עוֹלָם is time whose bounds are out of view: the far past (“the days of עוֹלָם”, Deu 32:7), and a future with no end in sight, which lasts as long as what it is said of lasts: a servant’s life (Exo 21:6), a child’s years at the sanctuary (1Sa 1:22, 28), Yahweh’s own kingdom without end (Exo 15:18; Psa 145:13). Its plural, “ages”, and the Aramaic and the Peshitta’s עָלְמָא, the word behind the New Testament’s “age(s)” and “eternal life”, carry it into the ages of God’s purpose (Dan 2:44; Heb 1:2). The verb עָלַם is to be hidden or to hide, most often to look away from what one ought to see (Lev 5:2–4; Deu 22:1–4); עֶלֶם and עַלְמָה are a young man and an unmarried young woman (1Sa 17:56; Gen 24:43; Isa 7:14). Cognates show two older roots in the one spelling: the time word with ʿ (Ugaritic ʿlm “eternity”) and the youth words with ġ (Ugaritic ġlm “boy”, Arabic ġulām); no cognate has been found for “hide”, so its tie to either is not established.

words.gloss: time out of sight; the age; of old; for ever
words.summary: Almost always with a preposition (לְעוֹלָם, עַד עוֹלָם, מֵעוֹלָם) or bound to a noun as “of עוֹלָם” (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם, בְּרִית עוֹלָם). It names duration reaching beyond what can be seen, backward or forward; how long it is in fact is set by what it is said of, so that it is a lifetime for a servant and without end for Yahweh. In Leviticus 23 each feast is a חֻקַּת עוֹלָם “throughout your generations” (Lev 23:14, 21, 31, 41).

senses.definition: The far past, beyond living memory: the days, paths, landmarks and ruins of עוֹלָם, and what has been so “from עוֹלָם”.

evidence.note: “Remember the days of עוֹלָם, consider the years of generation and generation; ask your father.” Parallel with the years of past generations.
The mighty men “who were from עוֹלָם, the men of the name”.
Your fathers dwelt beyond the River מֵעוֹלָם, Terah the father of Abraham.
“Ask for the paths of עוֹלָם, where the good way is.”
Do not move the boundary of עוֹלָם which your fathers set.
They will build the ruins of עוֹלָם.
He remembered the days of עוֹלָם, Moses and his people.
The ruler from Bethlehem, “whose goings out are from of old (מִקֶּדֶם), from the days of עוֹלָם”; Mat 2:6 quotes the verse’s first half.
The prophets who were before me and before you מִן הָעוֹלָם.
Those peoples were the inhabitants of the land מֵעוֹלָם.

senses.gloss: for as long as the bearer lasts; for life
senses.definition: Lasting with no end in view, where the end is in fact set by the life or state of the one it is said of: a servant’s service, a child given to the sanctuary, a slave held, a time in the deep.

evidence.note: The servant whose ear is bored “shall serve him לְעֹלָם”: for his life.
“He shall be your עֶבֶד עוֹלָם.”
Hannah: the boy shall appear before Yahweh “and dwell there עַד עוֹלָם”; in 1Sa 1:28 she says the same as “all the days that he lives”.
Achish: David “will be my servant לְעוֹלָם”.
Foreign slaves may be held לְעֹלָם.
“The earth with its bars was about me לְעוֹלָם”, of the three days in the fish (Jon 2:1): no end in sight to the one inside it.

senses.definition: Lasting without end, where what it is said of has none: Yahweh, his reign, his word, his covenant faithfulness, the king he promises David, and the life he gives at the resurrection.

evidence.note: “From עוֹלָם to עוֹלָם you are God”, before the mountains were born.
“Yahweh will reign לְעֹלָם וָעֶד.”
Lest the man take of the tree of life, eat, and live לְעֹלָם.
Abraham calls on the name of Yahweh, אֵל עוֹלָם.
Grass withers, “but the word of our God stands לְעוֹלָם”; quoted in 1Pe 1:24–25.
אֱלֹהֵי עוֹלָם does not faint or grow weary.
“I will establish the throne of his kingdom עַד עוֹלָם.”
“You are a priest לְעוֹלָם after the order of Melchizedek”, quoted in Heb 5:6; 7:17, 21, which reads it as “by the power of an endless life” (Heb 7:16).
“Your throne, O God, is עוֹלָם וָעֶד”, quoted of the Son in Heb 1:8.
The refrain “for his חֶסֶד is לְעוֹלָם”.
Of those who sleep in the dust some awake “to the life of עוֹלָם”, some to reproach and “abhorrence of עוֹלָם”.
Edom’s smoke goes up לְעוֹלָם, parallel with לְנֵצַח נְצָחִים: a desolation that will not be undone.

“He has put הָעֹלָם in their heart, yet so that man cannot find out the work God does from beginning to end.” The sense here is not settled: long duration set in man’s mind, or something hidden from him.

senses.definition: In the plural, the ages: spans of time one beyond another, past or to come, through which God and his works last.

evidence.note: “Your kingdom is a kingdom of all עֹלָמִים, and your dominion in every generation and generation.”
Israel saved by Yahweh with a salvation of עוֹלָמִים; “you shall not be ashamed עַד עוֹלְמֵי עַד”.
Solomon: a place for you to dwell עוֹלָמִים.
In Yah Yahweh is a rock of עוֹלָמִים.
Past ages: “it has been already לְעֹלָמִים which were before us”.
“The years of עוֹלָמִים”, the ages gone by.
At the end of the seventy weeks, to bring in צֶדֶק עֹלָמִים, a righteousness of the ages.

parallels.note: “Generation and generation” stands beside עוֹלָם as the long run of time.
“Before, of old”, set beside עוֹלָם of the past.
“Perpetuity”, joined with it in לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.

opposites.note: A moment of anger set against עוֹלָם of mercy.

phrases.gloss: a statute for the age, a lasting statute

evidence.note: The firstfruits: “a חֻקַּת עוֹלָם throughout your generations in all your dwellings”.
The Passover.

phrases.gloss: a covenant for the age, a lasting covenant
the mighty one of the age(s)
his house of the age: the grave

evidence.note: “Man goes to his בֵּית עוֹלָם”; Phoenician calls a tomb “house of ʿlm” the same way.

evidence.locator: Psa.110.4, לְעוֹלָם → εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα; Isa.40.8 and Psa.45.7 the same; αἰών renders עוֹלָם ×307

evidence.note: Psa 110:4 quoted: “a priest εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα”.
Isa 40:8 quoted: the word of the Lord remains εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
Psa 45:7 quoted of the Son.
Through the Son God made τοὺς αἰῶνας, the ages.
He will reign over the house of Jacob εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, the promise of 2Sa 7:13–16.

evidence.locator: Gen.17.7, בְּרִית עוֹלָם → διαθήκην αἰώνιον; Lev.23.14, חֻקַּת עוֹלָם → νόμιμον αἰώνιον; Dan.12.2, חַיֵּי עוֹלָם → ζωὴν αἰώνιον; αἰώνιος renders עוֹלָם ×101

evidence.note: “The blood of the διαθήκης αἰωνίου”: the בְּרִית עוֹלָם of Isa 55:3 and Ezk 37:26.
The righteous go into ζωὴν αἰώνιον, the חַיֵּי עוֹלָם of Dan 12:2.
Sodom and Gomorrah set forth as an example, undergoing the judgment of πυρὸς αἰωνίου; compare Zep 2:9, Moab to be like Sodom, “a desolation עַד עוֹלָם”.

words.gloss: be hidden; hide; hide oneself, look away
words.summary: Most of its uses are not of hiding a thing but of a matter being out of someone’s sight or knowledge (niphal), or of a person turning his eyes from what he should attend to (hiphil, hithpael). No cognate sharing this sense has been verified, so its tie to the rest of the root rests on the shared spelling alone.

stems.gloss: be hidden (from someone), be unknown to

senses.definition: Of a matter or a defilement that a person or the congregation does not see or know at the time, though it is true; the guilt stands when it becomes known.

evidence.note: The whole congregation errs “and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly”.
He touches an unclean thing “and it is hidden from him”; then he is guilty.
A rash oath “hidden from him”; “when he knows, he shall be guilty”.
Adultery “hidden from the eyes of her husband”.
No matter was hidden from the king that he did not tell the queen of Sheba.
Wisdom “is hidden from the eyes of all living”.
God will bring every deed into judgment, with every hidden thing, good or evil.
Nineveh “will be hidden”: brought to nothing, or forced into hiding.
Participle: “those who hide themselves”, dissemblers, beside men of falsehood.

stems.gloss: hide; hide one’s eyes or ear from

senses.gloss: hide one’s eyes from, refuse to see
senses.definition: Turn one’s eyes or ear away from what calls for action: a crime, the poor, a prayer; said also of Yahweh not hearing, and of a bribe that blinds.

evidence.note: If the people of the land “hide their eyes” from the man who gives his seed to Molech, and do not put him to death.
The priests “hid their eyes from my sabbaths”.
He who hides his eyes from the poor will have many curses.
Samuel: from whose hand have I taken a bribe “to blind my eyes with it”?
Yahweh: when you spread out your hands, “I will hide my eyes from you”.
“Do not hide your ear at my breathing, my cry.”
“Why do you hide in times of trouble?”

senses.definition: Keep something from being known.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
“Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge?”

senses.gloss: hide oneself from, look the other way
senses.definition: Hold oneself back from what one sees and ought to help: a brother’s strayed animal, the naked, one’s own flesh; of God, not to answer a plea.

evidence.note: You shall not see your brother’s ox or sheep driven away “and hide yourself from them”: you shall surely return them.
“You may not hide yourself.”
The fast Yahweh chooses: cover the naked, “and do not hide yourself from your own flesh”.
“Do not hide yourself from my plea.”
Of streams in which the snow “hides itself”.

senses.definition: The passive participle as a noun: what a person keeps hidden, laid open before God.

evidence.note: “You have set our iniquities before you, עֲלֻמֵנוּ in the light of your face”, parallel with “our iniquities”.

words.gloss: the age; of old; for ever (Aramaic)
words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra uses it as Hebrew uses עוֹלָם, mostly in the plural לְעָלְמִין, “to the ages”, of the kingdom God sets up and gives to the saints.

senses.definition: Without end: of the life wished to the king, of God’s name and kingdom, and of the kingdom given to the Son of Man and to the saints.

evidence.note: The God of heaven sets up a kingdom that will not be destroyed לְעָלְמִין, and it will stand לְעָלְמַיָּא.
To one like a son of man: “his dominion is a dominion of עָלַם which will not pass away”.
The saints of the Most High receive the kingdom “עַד עָלְמָא and עַד עָלַם עָלְמַיָּא”.
“Blessed be the name of God מִן עָלְמָא וְעַד עָלְמָא.”
His kingdom is a kingdom of עָלַם.
Nebuchadnezzar praises him who lives לְעָלְמָא.
“O king, live לְעָלְמִין!”, the court’s greeting.

senses.definition: In מִן יוֹמָת עָלְמָא, “from the days of old”.

evidence.note: The records show the city has rebelled “from the days of עָלְמָא”.

words.gloss: young woman, girl of marriageable age
words.summary: A girl grown to marriageable age and not yet married, as far as the verses that fix it show: Rebekah at the well, Miriam as a girl, and the עֲלָמוֹת set apart from the queens and concubines. Isaiah’s sign is that הָעַלְמָה will conceive and bear a son (Isa 7:14), which Matthew reads of Mary (Mat 1:23).

senses.definition: A young woman of marriageable age, not yet married.

evidence.note: The servant’s prayer for “the עַלְמָה who comes out to draw”; the same Rebekah is called a נַעֲרָה and a בְּתוּלָה “whom no man had known” (Gen 24:16).
Miriam, still a girl, goes to call the child’s mother.
Sixty queens, eighty concubines, “and עֲלָמוֹת without number”: young women distinct from wives.
“Therefore the עֲלָמוֹת love you.”
In the procession, “in the midst of עֲלָמוֹת playing timbrels”.
“The way of a man with an עַלְמָה”, one of four things too wonderful to know; the verse does not fix whether she is married.
“The Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, הָעַלְמָה will conceive and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel.” Quoted in Mat 1:23.

senses.definition: A heading for the singing or playing of a psalm, perhaps for young women’s voices; what it named is not known.

evidence.note: “A song עַל עֲלָמוֹת.”
Levites with harps עַל עֲלָמוֹת, beside others “on the eighth” (1Ch 15:21).

evidence.locator: Isa.7.14, הָעַלְמָה → ἡ παρθένος; Gen.24.43, הָעַלְמָה → ἡ παρθένος; Exo.2.8 has ἡ νεᾶνις

evidence.note: Isa 7:14 quoted: “Behold, ἡ παρθένος will conceive and bear a son”, of Mary, who conceived before she and Joseph came together (Mat 1:18).

words.summary: An abstract plural, the time and vigour of youth.

senses.definition: The years of youth, and the strength that belongs to them.

evidence.note: “You will forget the shame of your עֲלוּמִים”, parallel with “the reproach of your widowhood”.
“You have shortened the days of his עֲלוּמִים.”
His flesh fresher than a child’s; he returns to the days of his עֲלוּמִים.
“His bones are full of his עֲלוּמִים, but it lies down with him in the dust.”

words.summary: A noun of the verb “be hidden”: what lies out of sight, known to God. Like the verb, it has no cognate sharing its meaning.

senses.definition: What is hidden: the secrets of the heart, of wisdom, and what lies underground until it is brought to light.

evidence.note: “Would God not search this out? For he knows the תַּעֲלֻמוֹת of the heart.”
That God would show you the תַּעֲלֻמוֹת of wisdom.
Man in the mine “brings תַּעֲלֻמָהּ out to light”.

senses.definition: A youth; used beside נַעַר of the same person.

evidence.note: Saul: “Ask whose son this עָלֶם is”, of David, called a נַעַר in 1Sa 17:55, 58.
Jonathan’s arrow boy, called a נַעַר in the verse before.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s one word for both Greek αἰών, “age”, and κόσμος, “world”: “this age and the age to come”, “to the ages”, “life of the age” (ܚܝܐ ܕܠܥܠܡ, “eternal life”), and “God so loved the world”. SEDRA counts 413 uses in the New Testament.

senses.definition: A span of time in God’s ordering: this age, the age to come, the end of the age, the ages God made through the Son.

evidence.note: Not forgiven “in this עָלְמָא nor in the one to come”.
Through the Son he made the עָלְמֵא (τοὺς αἰῶνας).
The עָלְמֵא were framed by the word of God.
“I am with you … to the end of the עָלְמָא.”
The harvest is the end of the עָלְמָא.
Those counted worthy to attain “that עָלְמָא and the resurrection from the dead”.
At the end of the עָלְמֵא he appeared to put away sin.
To deliver us from this present evil עָלְמָא.

senses.definition: With לְ, for ever; and as “of לְעָלַם”, lasting, eternal: the life, redemption, covenant and spirit of the age.

evidence.note: Psa 110:4: a priest לְעָלַם.
He will reign over the house of Jacob לְעָלַם.
“Life of לְעָלַם”, ζωὴ αἰώνιος.
A redemption of לְעָלַם.
Through the spirit of לְעָלַם he offered himself without blemish.
The blood of the covenant of לְעָלַם.

senses.definition: The world and its people, rendering κόσμος; a sense biblical Hebrew עוֹלָם does not clearly show.

evidence.note: “God so loved the עָלְמָא.”
He was in the עָלְמָא, and the עָלְמָא was made through him, and the עָלְמָא did not know him.
“You are the light of the עָלְמָא.”

words.gloss: worldly way, course of this world (Peshitta)

senses.definition: The manner of the present age, rendering αἰών in “the course of this world”.

evidence.note: You walked “according to the עָלְמָיוּתָא of this world” (κατὰ τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ κόσμου).

senses.definition: Belonging to the present world, rendering κοσμικός.

evidence.note: The first covenant had ordinances of service and a holy place that was עָלְמָנָיָא, “worldly”.

senses.definition: A young man, rendering νεανίσκος and νεανίας; in the plural, the younger men.

evidence.note: A certain עְלַיְמָא followed him, a linen cloth about him.
In the tomb they saw a עְלַיְמָא sitting on the right.
At Nain: “עְלַיְמָא, I say to you, arise.”
Eutychus.
Saul, a עְלַיְמָא, keeps the clothes at Stephen’s death.
“I write to you, עְלַיְמֵא, because you have overcome the evil one.”

words.summary: In the Peshitta a servant girl, rendering παιδίσκη. Mat 1:23, quoting Isa 7:14, uses not this word but ܒܬܘܠܬܐ, “virgin”.

senses.definition: A young woman in service.

evidence.note: One of the high priest’s עְלַיְמָתָא comes to Peter.
A עְלַיְמְתָא with a spirit of divination, who brought her masters gain.

cognates.gloss: unlimited time, eternity; ʿd ʿlm “for ever”
cognates.note: Ugaritic writes ʿ and ġ with different letters, and this word has ʿ: the time sense of the root goes back to ʿlm, not ġlm. The same page lists ʿlmt /ʿulmat-/ “future”, šḥr ʿlmt “tomorrow and in the future” (KTU 3.5:15).

evidence.note: “ʿlm ‘unlimited time, eternity’; ʿlmh 1.23:49 = 88.2, 1.19:IV:6 = 87.4 ‘to eternity’; ʿd ʿlm 3.5:14 … (cf. H. ʿōlām, Aram., Arab. ʿālam)”.

cognates.gloss: eternity; bt ʿlm “house of eternity”, a tomb; l ʿlm “for ever”
cognates.note: A resting-place “of peace for ʿlm” (KAI 35); the tomb as “house of ʿlm” answers to Ecc 12:5, בֵּית עוֹלָמוֹ. Phoenician writes ʿ and ġ alike, so it shows nothing of the older sound.

evidence.note: “n.m. 1. ETERNITY”, KAI 35.1/2; “See also BT ʿLM, ‘tomb (lit., house of eternity)’; ʿD ʿLM, ‘always’; L ʿLM, ‘forever’.”

cognates.note: The Targums render Hebrew עוֹלָם by it (Targ. Gen 9:16; Targ. Onqelos Exo 21:6, where the servant serves לְעֹלָם); later Aramaic also uses it for “the world”, as the Peshitta does.

evidence.note: “= h. עוֹלָם, eternity, world &c. Targ. Gen. IX, 16. Targ. O. Ex. XXI, 6. Targ. Ps. LXI, 7.”

cognates.gloss: the world, the creation, all created beings
cognates.note: Lane’s sources derive it from عِلْم “knowledge”, as “that by means of which one knows [the Creator]”, and give it only the sense “world, creation”, never “eternity” or “age”. Its sense matches later Aramaic עָלְמָא “world”, and it may be a borrowing from Aramaic; that has not been checked in an Arabic etymological source. Recorded as possible: if native, it shows ʿ, agreeing with Ugaritic ʿlm.

evidence.note: “A name for That by means of which one knows [a thing] … or it signifies الخَلْقُ [the creation] … [it may often be rendered the world]”.

cognates.note: Ugaritic has ġ, not ʿ, in the youth words, against ʿ in ʿlm “eternity”: two older roots behind one Hebrew spelling. Segert gives H. ʿælæm beside ġlm and H. ʿalmā beside ġlmt.

evidence.note: “ġlm ‘boy’ (H. ʿælæm; cf. Syr. ʿlaymā, Arab. ġulām)”; “ġlmt ‘girl’ 1.14:IV:41 = 88.72 (H. ʿalmā)”.

cognates.gloss: young man, youth, boy; a servant
cognates.note: Arabic keeps غ apart from ع, and the youth word has غ. Lane also records غُلُومَةٌ, the state of a ġulām, and notes a rare عُلَام for غُلَام “by substitution of ع for غ” (p. 2140, n30356), a late Arabic interchange, not the Hebrew merger.

evidence.note: “[A young man, youth, boy, or male child:] … one from the time of his birth until he attains to the period termed شَبَاب … It is also used as meaning … A male slave”; feminine غُلَامَةٌ in poetry.

cognates.note: Old South Arabian keeps ġ apart, and has it here, agreeing with Ugaritic and Arabic.

evidence.note: “CHILD, BOY, YOUTH [Ar ġulām ‘boy, youth,’ Heb ʿelem ‘young man.’]”; C19/7–8 ġlm wldthw M “the boy M. bore (to) him”.

cognates.gloss: young woman; maidens offered in the Kition temple
cognates.note: Kilamuwa: “one used to barter a girl (ʿlmt) for a lamb”. Phoenician writes ʿ and ġ alike.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ʿalma] n.f. 1. YOUNG WOMAN” KAI 24.8; “2. VIRGIN offered in sacrifice in the Astarte temple in Kition” KAI 37 B 9.

cognates.gloss: young man, lad; servant; feminine עוּלֵימְתָּא girl
cognates.note: Targum Onqelos uses it in Gen 41:12 and the feminine in Gen 24:14; Targum Samuel in 1Sa 17:55.

evidence.note: “young, young man; servant. Targ. II Chr. XXXV, 27 … Targ. O. Gen. XLI, 12 … Targ. I Sam. XVII, 55 … Fem. עוּלֵימְתָּא … Targ. O. Gen. XXIV, 14.”

cognates.note: Listed only in Anderson and Moser’s root database; not checked in Dillmann or Leslau. Geʿez merged ġ into ʿ, so it could not show the older sound in any case.

doctrine.statement: Scripture speaks of time as ages, one beyond another: Yahweh is God “from עוֹלָם to עוֹלָם” (Psa 90:2), and his kingdom is “a kingdom of all עֹלָמִים” (Psa 145:13). Daniel sees the God of heaven set up a kingdom that stands לְעָלְמִין and is given to one like a son of man and to the saints of the Most High (Dan 2:44; 7:14, 18, 27), and he is told of an awakening from the dust to “the life of עוֹלָם” (Dan 12:2). The New Testament, and the Peshitta in the same word עָלְמָא, says that God made the ages through the Son (Heb 1:2) and framed them by his word (Heb 11:3); it sets “this age” against “the age to come” (Mat 12:32), says those counted worthy to attain “that age and the resurrection from the dead” die no more (Luk 20:35–36), and says Christ appeared once “at the end of the ages” to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself (Heb 9:26). From the verses: the ages are ordered by God’s purpose in his Son, and the life of the age (ζωὴ αἰώνιος, ܚܝܐ ܕܠܥܠܡ) is the life of the kingdom Daniel saw, entered by resurrection at the last day (Jhn 6:40).

Yahweh made with Abraham a בְּרִית עוֹלָם, to be God to him and to his seed after him, and gave him and his seed the land of Canaan as an אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם (Gen 17:7–8; 13:15). With David he made a covenant of a house and a throne established עַד עוֹלָם (2Sa 7:13, 16), which David calls a בְּרִית עוֹלָם (2Sa 23:5) and Isaiah offers to all who come as “a בְּרִית עוֹלָם, the sure mercies of David” (Isa 55:3); Jeremiah and Ezekiel promise a בְּרִית עוֹלָם of peace that will not turn away from Israel (Jer 32:40; Ezk 37:26). The New Testament says the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed, “who is Christ” (Gal 3:16); that the son of Mary will be given the throne of his father David and reign over the house of Jacob for the ages (Luk 1:32–33); that the holy things of David are given in his resurrection (Act 13:34, quoting Isa 55:3); and that God raised him from the dead “by the blood of the everlasting covenant” (Heb 13:20). From the verses: the covenant עוֹלָם is the promise to Abraham and David, kept in Christ and lasting as long as he lives, who “dies no more” (Rom 6:9).

Each appointed time of Leviticus 23 is “a חֻקַּת עוֹלָם throughout your generations in all your dwellings” (Lev 23:14, 21, 31, 41), as the Passover is (Exo 12:14), and Aaron’s sons are given “a כְּהֻנַּת עוֹלָם throughout their generations” (Exo 40:15; Num 25:13). Yet the same scriptures promise another priest לְעוֹלָם, after the order of Melchizedek (Psa 110:4), and Hebrews reasons from it that the priesthood has been changed, and with it the law (Heb 7:11–12, 17, 24). Paul calls feast days, new moons and sabbaths “a shadow of the things to come; the body is of Christ” (Col 2:16–17), Hebrews calls the law “a shadow of the good things to come” (Heb 10:1), and Christ is called “our Passover, sacrificed for us” (1Co 5:7). From the verses: a statute עוֹלָם lasted, as the word allows, for the age it belonged to, “throughout your generations”, and the New Testament finds its substance in Christ, whose priesthood is by “an endless life” (Heb 7:16).

Ahaz is given a sign from Yahweh himself: “behold, הָעַלְמָה will conceive and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel” (Isa 7:14). Where the text shows who an עַלְמָה is, she is a girl not yet married: Rebekah at the well, who is also called a בְּתוּלָה “whom no man had known” (Gen 24:16, 43), Miriam as a girl (Exo 2:8), and the עֲלָמוֹת set apart from queens and concubines (Sng 6:8). Matthew tells that Mary was found with child of the holy spirit before she and Joseph came together, and that this fulfilled Isa 7:14, “the virgin will conceive” (Mat 1:18–23); Luke tells it independently, of a παρθένος betrothed to Joseph who asks “How will this be, since I know not a man?” (Luk 1:27, 34–35). From the verses: the son of the sign was born of a young woman who had not known a man, by the power of the Most High, and so is “Son of God” (Luk 1:35).

The plural עֲלָמוֹת in Psa 46:1 and 1Ch 15:20 is kept as a sense of עַלְמָה, as BDB’s key counts it. Merged letter ע: the time word shows ʿ (Ugaritic ʿlm, and Arabic ʿālam if native); the youth words show ġ (Ugaritic ġlm, ġlmt; Arabic ġulām; Sabaic ġlm); no cognate shows the sound behind the verb “hide”, so whether “hidden” and “time out of view” are one older root is not shown by the cognates either way, and the verses never tie them. Anderson and Moser put all three under one *ġlm, against Ugaritic ʿlm for the time word; the entry follows the Ugaritic spelling. The Peshitta does not use ʿlm for “hide” (Payne Smith p. 415 has only the Palpel “blow away”, not entered), and renders Isa 7:14 at Mat 1:23 by ܒܬܘܠܬܐ, not ܥܠܝܡܬܐ.
